title: An RNA-immunoprecipitation protocol to identify RNAs associated with RNA-binding proteins in cytoplasmic and nuclear Drosophila head fractions
protocol: Collect and freeze adult flies.
Transfer 5-7 day-old anesthetized flies into 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Snap freeze flies by immediately plunging the tubes into liquid nitrogen.
Vortex the tubes for 15 s and shake vigorously to separate the heads, legs, and wings from the bodies.
Repeat vortexing and shaking twice or thrice.
Assemble the sieves pre-chilled at -20°C together, with the sieve having a bigger mesh size (630 μm) on top of the one with a smaller mesh size (400 μm).
Transfer the frozen fly material to the assembled sieves.
Sift by vigorous shaking to separate fly bodies and heads.
Retain fly bodies on the top sieve.
Retain fly heads on the bottom sieve.
Transfer the head fraction to 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes using a funnel pre-chilled at −20°C.
Use a brush for transferring the head fraction.
Prepare aliquots of 1 mL heads.
Store the collected head fractions at −80°C.
Grind fly heads in a mortar and pestle cooled with liquid nitrogen.
Grind fly heads into a fine powder using a liquid nitrogen-cooled mortar and pestle.
Transfer the powdered fly heads to a pre-chilled 15 mL Dounce homogenizer.
Add 8.5 mL of ice-cold Lysis Buffer containing RNaseOUT, protease inhibitors, and DTT.
Homogenize the mixture by pushing the pestle up and down several times until the solution becomes opaque.
Transfer the homogenate to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 100 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 15 mL Falcon tube.
Save two aliquots: one of 100 μL for RNA extraction and one of 50 μL for protein extraction.
Separate cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions by centrifuging at 900 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant (cytoplasmic fraction) into a new 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Discard the remaining pelleted debris and transfer the supernatant to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Save two aliquots: one of 100 μL for RNA extraction and one of 50 μL for protein extraction.
Wash the pellet recovered after step 9 in 1 mL of Sucrose Buffer (+ RNaseOUT + protease inhibitors + DTT).
Centrifuge at 900 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of Sucrose Buffer (+ RNaseOUT + protease inhibitors + DTT) supplemented with 800 μL of High Salt Buffer (+ RNaseOUT + protease inhibitors + DTT).
Incubate for 30 min on ice, inverting the tube every 5 min.
Digest DNA.
Add 4.6 mL of Sucrose Buffer supplemented with RNaseOUT, protease inhibitors, and DTT.
Add 7.5 μL of CaCl2 1 M to reach a final concentration of 150 mM NaCl and 1 mM CaCl2.
Invert the tube several times after addition.
Pipette 75 μL of DNaseI into the mixture and invert the tube again.
Incubate for 15 min at 37°C, agitating every 5 min.
Add 60 μL of EDTA 0.5 M to stop the reaction and reach a final concentration of 4 mM.
Invert the tube 5 times after addition.
Centrifuge the mixture at 16,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant (soluble nuclear fraction) into a 15 mL Falcon tube on ice.
Save two aliquots: one of 100 μL for RNA extraction and another of 50 μL for protein extraction.
If desired, transfer 50 μL of the nuclear fraction collected in step 11.c.iii to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge this Eppendorf tube at 16,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet into 50 μL of urea buffer to prepare an aliquot corresponding to the nuclear insoluble fraction.
Pre-clear the cytoplasmic and soluble nuclear fractions.
Prepare control agarose beads.
Transfer the beads to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Calculate the total amount of agarose beads needed.
Pipette the corresponding volume with a pre-cut tip.
Add 500 μL of Lysis Buffer per 120 μL of beads.
Gently tap the tube and centrifuge at 400 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps two more times.
Add 500 μL of Lysis Buffer per 120 μL of beads again.
Pipette up and down several times to resuspend.
Split into independent 15 mL Falcon tubes based on conditions.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 2 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads by gently tapping the tubes.
Transfer each nuclear and cytoplasmic fraction to one of the prepared Falcon Tubes.
Agitate on a nutator for 30 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Immunoprecipitate GFP-tagged proteins from cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions.
Transfer each of the pre-cleared supernatant recovered in step 12.b to one of the individual Falcon Tubes prepared in step 13.a.
Resuspend the beads by gently tapping the tubes.
Agitate on a nutator for 1 h 30 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 2 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Save two aliquots of the supernatant: one of 100 μL for RNA extraction and one of 50 μL for protein extraction.
Add 500 μL of Lysis Buffer (+ RNaseOUT + protease inhibitors + DTT) and resuspend the beads by gently tapping the tubes.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 2 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps 14.a and 14.b three times.
Transfer the resuspended bead solution to a 1.5 mL low binding Eppendorf tube.
Save an aliquot of 20 μL for protein extraction.
Resuspend the beads in 100 μL of Lysis Buffer (+ RNaseOUT + protease inhibitors + DTT).
Digest proteins by adding 1.5 μL of Proteinase K solution and incubating for 30 min at 55°C in a Thermomixer under agitation.
Gently tap the tubes 3–4 times during the incubation.
Collect the supernatant in a 1.5 mL low binding Eppendorf tube.
Add 600 μL of TRI Reagent to each tube and mix by pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Add 150 μL of chloroform to the tubes.
Shake the tubes vigorously for 15 s.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 10–15 min at 4°C.
Tilt the tube and pipette the aqueous phase into a 1.5 mL low binding Eppendorf tube.
Add 1.5 μL of GlycoBlue to the aqueous phase.
Add an equivalent volume (about 500 μL) of isopropanol and vortex for 5–10 s.
Precipitate RNA overnight (∼12–16 h) at −20°C.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 25 minutes at 4°C.
Add 600 μL of 70% ethanol.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove and discard the supernatant without touching the pellet.
Centrifuge briefly to remove potential remaining ethanol.
Let the pellet dry for 5–10 minutes at room temperature.
Resuspend the RNA pellet.
Add 20 μL of RNase-free water and pipet up and down until dissolution of the pellet.
Save 2–3 μL for quality check.
Mount the gel in the electrophoresis chamber.
Fill the chamber with running buffer.
Load samples on the gel (35 μL), including a molecular weight marker.
Run the gel for 1 h 30 min at 110 V.
Cut a gel-sized PVDF membrane and activate it with methanol for 1 min.
Prepare the transfer sandwich in the gel holder cassette by positioning the gel and the membrane between foam pads and filter papers.
Place the cassette in the electrophoresis chamber and fill the chamber with transfer buffer.
Transfer overnight (∼12–16 h) at 40 mA at 4°C.
Rinse the membrane with PBS.
Block the membrane with blocking buffer for 1 h at room temperature under agitation.
Incubate the membrane with primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer overnight (∼12–16 h), at 4°C, under agitation.
Wash the membrane three times with PBS-Tween for 10 min at room temperature under agitation.
Incubate the membrane with fluorescent secondary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer for 2 h at room temperature, under agitation.
Protect from light during incubation to avoid exciting the antibodies with ambient light.
Wash the membrane three times for 10 min with PBS-Tween at room temperature under agitation.
Image using a fluorescence Odyssey imaging system.
Assess RNA quality.
Measure the concentration of RNA samples using the QuBit RNA high sensitivity assay, according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute RNA samples with commercial RNAse-free water if the concentration is higher than 1 ng/μL to reach a concentration of 1 ng/μL.
Determine the integrity of RNA samples with an Agilent bioanalyzer.
Use the Agilent RNA 6000 Pico Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
